hero.headline: Pakistan announces US and Iran reach agreement to end conflict
hero.body:
Pakistan's prime minister declared on Friday that the United States and Iran have reached an agreement on a peace framework to end their conflict, which has lasted more than 100 days. Pakistan has been leading mediation efforts between the two countries to halt hostilities in the Middle East and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

The announcement came after President Donald Trump stated that the two nations were on the verge of signing a peace agreement and cancelled planned missile strikes on Iran. However, Iranian officials quickly challenged Trump's characterization of the deal's status, creating conflicting narratives about whether a final agreement had actually been reached.

Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said that "exchanges of messages are continuing, but no final agreement has been reached yet." The semi-official Tasnim news agency reported that Trump's announcement was "in line with his usual pattern of making unilateral and egotistical statements."

Trump outlined his conditions for the deal on his Truth Social platform, stating that Iran "must agree that they will never have a Nuclear Weapon or Bomb." He also listed opening the Strait of Hormuz for all traffic without tolls, eliminating mines in the waterway, and allowing the United States to remove and destroy highly enriched uranium from a secure nuclear site in Iran. The deal would also block the transfer of frozen assets to Iran, according to Trump.

Vice President JD Vance pushed back against details that Iranian officials had leaked about the proposed agreement, insisting that Iran would not receive any cash under its terms. The Trump administration dismissed information that Tehran had released about the possible memorandum of understanding.

Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi struck a more optimistic tone, stating that an agreement to extend the ceasefire, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and launch negotiations on Iran's nuclear program has "never been closer to completion." His remarks represented the most hopeful assessment yet from Tehran about finalizing a deal in the coming days.

Iran's top negotiator Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf sent a defiant message, stating that "we seize concessions not through dialogue, but with missiles." He also warned that Iran was ready for another round of fighting if talks to extend the ceasefire failed.

The proposed framework addresses multiple aspects of the conflict between the two nations. Beyond ending immediate hostilities, the agreement would tackle access through the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for global oil shipments. Discussions on Iran's nuclear program indicate the diplomatic effort extends beyond the military confrontation to address longer-term security concerns that have defined US-Iran relations for decades.

A meeting in Washington between US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar ended without public comment on the negotiations.

cards.headline: Scientists Begin Testing Treatments as Ebola Outbreak Spreads
cards.teaser: Trials are starting on several drugs that showed promise in preliminary studies against the virus causing the current outbreak.
cards.body:
Medical researchers have begun clinical trials on multiple treatments for the Ebola virus as the outbreak expands across affected regions. Several drugs demonstrated encouraging results in early-stage studies, prompting authorities to accelerate testing.

The trials represent a race to find effective therapies as case numbers rise. Scientists are working to determine which treatments can reduce mortality and slow transmission of the virus that is driving the current epidemic.

cards.headline: One dead, nine wounded in Midland, Texas mass shooting; suspect killed
cards.body:
A shooting in Midland, Texas on Friday left one person dead and nine others injured, according to city authorities. The suspected shooter engaged in a standoff with police for approximately two hours before being killed later that afternoon.

Law enforcement responded to reports of gunfire in an industrial area of the city shortly after 8 a.m. local time. Midland Mayor Lori Blong confirmed the incident on Friday morning. The shooting eventually ended near a veterinary hospital in the area.

Witnesses reported hearing what sounded like at least 40 shots fired during the incident. Andrea Mendias, who works at an auto body shop near the veterinary hospital, provided video footage showing officers emerging from an armored police vehicle and law enforcement deploying robots in the surrounding area.

All nine injured victims were transported to Midland Memorial Hospital for treatment. Hospital officials reported that four patients were in operating rooms receiving emergency care, while five others were in stable condition. The hospital's emergency department was placed on lockdown as a security precaution.

Midland is located approximately 300 miles west of Fort Worth and Dallas in the heart of Texas's oil region. The city has a population of about 140,000 residents.

The shooting marks another violent incident in a community with recent experience of mass casualty events. Six years ago, a gunman who had been fired from an oil services job carried out a shooting rampage across the Odessa and Midland areas, killing seven people and wounding two dozen others as he fired at random while driving through the region.

Authorities continued investigating the circumstances of Friday's shooting, working to establish a timeline of events and determine the suspect's motive. No information was released regarding the identities of the victims or the shooter at the time of reporting.

The incident adds to a troubling pattern of mass shootings across Texas in recent years, reigniting national conversations about gun violence and public safety. The state has experienced multiple high-profile mass casualty events, including shootings in El Paso, Uvalde, and Sutherland Springs.

Law enforcement agencies worked to piece together details about how the shooting unfolded and what circumstances led to the violence. The standoff between the suspect and police lasted roughly two hours before ending with the suspect's death, effectively concluding the active threat to the community.

cards.headline: Massive warehouse fire burns at Tracy medical supply facility, disrupts western US supply chain
cards.teaser: A fire at a one million square foot Medline Industries warehouse in Tracy, California continues to burn, with crews expecting to work for days.
cards.body:
A massive fire destroyed a one million square-foot medical equipment warehouse in Tracy, California, early Friday. The blaze sent thick black smoke billowing into the air as firefighters battled the flames. Authorities evacuated nearby facilities, though no injuries were reported.

The facility, operated by Medline Industries, serves as a major distribution hub for medical products across the western United States. The fire has disrupted the regional medical supply chain, with crews expected to remain on scene for multiple days as they work to fully contain the blaze.

cards.headline: Israel Constructs Military Base in Jenin Despite 1990s Agreement
cards.teaser: The army base in the West Bank city defies an accord with Palestinians, drawing criticism that it will facilitate settlement expansion.
cards.body:
Israel has built a new military base in Jenin, a move critics say violates agreements reached with Palestinians in the 1990s. The construction occurred in a Palestinian population center in the West Bank.

Opponents of the base say the facility will enable the Israeli military to protect increased settlement activity near Palestinian communities. The construction represents a departure from commitments made in earlier peace accords that limited Israeli military presence in certain areas.

cards.headline: Federal judge extends block on Trump administration anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: A federal judge indefinitely blocked the Trump administration's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund, saying she wants guarantees the program has been abandoned.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Virginia extended an order blocking the Trump administration's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund. The fund was created to resolve a lawsuit against the IRS over the leak of Trump's tax returns. Judge Leonie Brinkema said the administration's public statements that the fund was discontinued were insufficient.

The judge indicated she would lift the order if the acting attorney general and treasury secretary filed a declaration under penalty of perjury within a week confirming the fund would not proceed. The block remains in place while legal challenges continue.

cards.headline: SpaceX Stock Jumps 11% in Largest IPO Ever
cards.body:
SpaceX began trading publicly on Friday with shares opening at $150, representing an 11% increase from the $135 initial pricing. The debut marked the largest initial public offering in history, with the company raising $75 billion and achieving a valuation above $1.77 trillion.

The successful market launch created an immediate windfall for Elon Musk, the company's founder and majority shareholder. With roughly 85% of SpaceX's voting shares, Musk's net worth climbed to approximately $1.1 trillion, making him the world's first trillionaire. His total wealth includes roughly $300 billion from his stake in Tesla, valued at $1.2 trillion.

The trading debut included ceremonial elements reflecting SpaceX's cultural significance. Executives rang the opening bell at the Nasdaq exchange as Elton John's "Rocket Man" played. Musk addressed the occasion at SpaceX's headquarters, emphasizing the company's mission to "make humanity multiplanetary" and "take the fiction out of science fiction." SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell announced that the company had launched a Falcon 9 rocket that morning from Cape Canaveral, deploying 29 Starlink satellites into orbit.

The IPO followed an unusual process. Rather than offering a price range to gauge investor demand, SpaceX set a fixed price of $135 per share on an accept-it-or-leave-it basis. Reports indicated investor demand reached four times the oversubscribed level, potentially generating up to $250 billion in total investment interest. This extraordinary demand prompted scrutiny from Senator Elizabeth Warren, who called on the Securities and Exchange Commission to investigate whether SpaceX's valuation contained "inaccurate or misleading" accounting.

Analysts have highlighted concerns about SpaceX's financial fundamentals. The company generated $18.7 billion in revenue last year while recording a $4.3 billion operating loss. Additionally, SpaceX's governance structure concentrates significant power in Musk's hands, and the company is investing heavily in AI infrastructure through xAI's datacenter buildout.

The IPO will have broad implications for average investors. SpaceX shares will enter index funds on an accelerated timeline, faster than typical for newly public companies. This means retirement accounts and pension plans will gain automatic exposure to SpaceX, giving millions of Americans indirect stakes in the company regardless of whether they actively chose to invest.

For SpaceX employees, the IPO created substantial wealth. More than 4,400 current and former employees are expected to become millionaires, with 400 individuals each securing $100 million or more.

The SpaceX offering occurs amid a broader wave of technology company IPOs. OpenAI and Anthropic have filed to go public this year and are predicted to raise sums nearing $1 trillion combined, further concentrating market attention and investor capital on artificial intelligence companies.

hero.headline: Pakistan Says Final Text of US-Iran Peace Deal Agreed
hero.teaser: Pakistan's prime minister announced that the final text of a peace deal between the United States and Iran has been reached, marking a potential end to ongoing .
hero.body:
President Trump announced Thursday that the US and Iran are on the verge of signing a peace agreement and cancelled planned missile strikes. Iran's foreign minister said an agreement "has never been closer," while Pakistan's prime minister claimed negotiators have reached a final, agreed-upon text of the deal.

However, Iran's foreign ministry dismissed Trump's claims, stating that a final decision on an agreement has not yet been made. The conflicting accounts highlight the fragile state of negotiations as both sides navigate diplomatic discussions following recent escalating attacks and a threatened ceasefire collapse.

cards.headline: Anti-Immigrant Violence in Belfast After Stabbing Leaves City Tense
cards.teaser: Two nights of riots in Northern Ireland saw people targeted based on skin color following a brutal stabbing incident.
cards.body:
Northern Ireland authorities said people were attacked because of their skin color during two nights of violence that erupted in Belfast following a stabbing incident. The riots have left the city on edge.

Police and local officials are working to restore calm and prevent further outbreaks of violence while protecting residents who were targeted during the unrest.

cards.headline: Families Mark One Year Since Air India Crash That Killed 260
cards.teaser: Relatives returned to Ahmedabad to honor those who died in the June 2025 disaster, but no investigative report has been released.
cards.body:
Grieving relatives gathered in Ahmedabad to commemorate the 260 lives lost when an Air India flight crashed in June 2025. The anniversary marked a year since the disaster that claimed the lives of passengers and crew.

Officials overseeing the investigation stated that "significant progress" has been made into determining what caused the crash. However, the official inquiry report has not yet been released, leaving families of victims still waiting for answers about the circumstances surrounding the disaster.

cards.headline: Mother Finds Son's Body After Kenya Ebola Quarantine Protests
cards.teaser: A woman located her missing son two days after demonstrations at a quarantine facility in Nanyuki.
cards.body:
Sylvester Muigai Ndung'u's mother found his body two days after protests erupted at a Kenyan Ebola quarantine center. The young man had traveled to Nanyuki to collect a school uniform when he went missing.

The discovery followed demonstrations at the quarantine facility where tensions had risen over containment measures. His mother said he had been in the town for a routine errand when he disappeared during the unrest.

cards.headline: French Town Buries Murdered Child as Police Failings Questioned
cards.teaser: The prime suspect in the killing of 11-year-old Lyhanna had been reported to police nine months earlier but was never questioned.
cards.body:
A French community mourned the death of Lyhanna, an 11-year-old girl who was killed. The case has sparked scrutiny of law enforcement's response to prior warnings about the main suspect.

Police had received a report about the individual nine months before the murder but never questioned him. The failure to follow up on this advance warning has raised serious questions about missed opportunities that could have prevented the child's death.

cards.headline: Man detained by ICE at Trump hotel in Doral after taking wife to president's property
cards.teaser: A man was detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement after taking his wife, a Trump supporter, to the president's hotel in Doral, Florida.
cards.body:
A man who brought his wife to the Trump National Doral Miami resort was detained by ICE agents at the property. His wife is reported to be a supporter of President Trump.

The detention occurred at the hotel owned by the president in Doral, Florida. The circumstances of the ICE operation at the Trump property and the man's immigration status were detailed in reporting by NBC News.

cards.headline: China detains US scholar Min Zin on suspicion of espionage
cards.teaser: Chinese authorities arrested Min Zin, an American scholar who leads a Myanmar-focused think tank, on suspicion of spying and endangering national security.
cards.body:
China's government detained Min Zin, a U.S. scholar who heads a think tank focused on Myanmar issues, on suspicion of engaging in espionage and endangering national security. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian announced the arrest on Friday.

Min Zin writes about Myanmar and Chinese foreign policy. His detention represents another case of a foreign national arrested in China on national security grounds.

cards.headline: Trump administration says Iran peace deal likely within days but not certain
cards.teaser: A senior US official expressed 80 to 85 percent confidence that a deal with Iran will be signed soon, though cautioned it is not guaranteed.
cards.body:
President Trump announced that the US and Iran are on the verge of signing a peace agreement and cancelled planned missile strikes following two days of escalating attacks. He claimed progress toward a deal after the ceasefire threatened to collapse.

Iran's foreign ministry dismissed Trump's assertion, stating that no final decision on an agreement has been reached. Both Iran and Pakistan separately said a deal has never been closer, echoing Trump's earlier statements about the negotiations.

cards.headline: Artist David Hockney dies at 88
cards.teaser: British artist David Hockney died at age 88, prompting tributes from King Charles and figures across the art world.
cards.body:
David Hockney, Britain's greatest artist, has died at the age of 88. The Bradford-born painter was one of the most influential artists of the modern era, known for his vivid and innovative work spanning more than six decades. His iconic paintings ranged from celebrated swimming pool scenes to portraits of American celebrities.

King Charles paid tribute to Hockney, describing him as a giant of the art world and one of life's true originals. The proud Yorkshireman's death prompted widespread recognition of his profound influence on contemporary art and his status as a household name.

cards.headline: Broader Markets Rise on SpaceX Debut and Iran Deal Hopes
cards.teaser: The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 370 points as investors responded to the SpaceX IPO and progress on a potential US-Iran agreement.
cards.body:
Major US stock indexes climbed as SpaceX made its market debut, with the Dow gaining 370 points. The record-breaking IPO valued SpaceX at $1.77 trillion after raising $75 billion. The company's fast-track inclusion on the Nasdaq triggered significant buying pressure from tracker funds and other forced buyers.

Oil prices fell following reports of advancing US-Iran negotiations and Trump's cancellation of further Iran strikes, reducing geopolitical tensions around the Strait of Hormuz. European stocks also posted strong gains on the peace deal prospects. The dual catalysts of a major technology IPO and improved diplomatic relations drove broader market optimism.

cards.headline: Musk Becomes First Trillionaire as SpaceX Shares Soar
cards.teaser: Elon Musk's net worth crossed one trillion dollars as SpaceX stock surged on its first day of trading.
cards.body:
Elon Musk has become the world's first trillionaire following SpaceX's historic initial public offering. The record-breaking IPO valued the rocket company at $1.77 trillion and raised $75 billion through its share offering. The surge in SpaceX's stock price on its market debut significantly boosted Musk's paper wealth past the one trillion dollar threshold.

SpaceX gained fast-track inclusion on the Nasdaq after the exchange modified its rules, guaranteeing substantial buying pressure from tracker funds and other index-linked investors. The company's weighting in the index could prove significant as trading continues.

cards.headline: AI Company IPOs Expected to Create About 20 New Billionaires
cards.teaser: Upcoming public offerings from Anthropic and OpenAI could mint approximately 20 new billionaires from employee equity stakes.
cards.body:
The wave of technology company IPOs beginning with SpaceX is expected to create about 20 new billionaires across three major offerings. Anthropic and OpenAI are preparing to follow SpaceX to public markets, and employees at all three companies hold equity stakes that will convert to publicly tradable shares.

Many more employees at these companies are positioned to become millionaires through their stock holdings. The wealth creation reflects both the high valuations these technology companies command and the equity compensation structures common in the industry. Early employees and executives who joined when the companies were private stand to see the largest gains as their shares begin trading on public exchanges.

cards.headline: SpaceX Receives Sell Rating from CFRA Shortly After IPO
cards.teaser: Research firm CFRA issued a sell rating on SpaceX stock hours after the company began trading publicly.
cards.body:
SpaceX's initial public offering raised approximately $75 billion, making it one of the largest IPOs ever. Shares were priced at $135 each and soared following their market debut, with the company reaching a valuation of roughly $1.77 trillion. The strong investor demand lifted Elon Musk's net worth into the trillionaire range.

Despite the bullish market response, CFRA issued a sell rating on the stock shortly after the IPO. The rating reflected analyst concerns about valuation levels as shares traded significantly above their offering price. The divergence highlighted how different research firms assess newly public companies differently as they evaluate business prospects and whether current prices reflect fair value.

cards.headline: SpaceX Shares to Enter Index Funds and 401(k) Accounts
cards.teaser: Retirement account holders with index funds will soon automatically own SpaceX shares as the company joins major market indexes.
cards.body:
Investors who hold index funds in retirement accounts like 401(k) plans will soon gain exposure to SpaceX whether they made an active choice to invest or not. Major stock market indexes that track the broader market add companies based on size and other criteria, and SpaceX's scale means it will qualify for inclusion.

Index funds that mirror these benchmarks must then purchase shares to match the index composition. This automatic inclusion means millions of Americans with passive investment strategies in their retirement accounts will become SpaceX shareholders. The company's weight in these indexes will depend on its total market value and the number of shares available for public trading.

cards.headline: Musk Posts on Politics and Culture During SpaceX IPO
cards.teaser: Elon Musk continued posting about political and cultural topics on social media as his rocket company went public.
cards.body:
SpaceX began trading publicly on the Nasdaq following a record-breaking initial public offering that valued the company at approximately $1.77 trillion. The offering raised $75 billion through share sales priced at $135 each, instantly making Elon Musk the world's first trillionaire as his net worth surged into the $1 trillion range.

The stock surged on its market debut, supported by forced buying from index tracker funds after the Nasdaq fast-tracked SpaceX's inclusion. The record IPO is expected to pave the way for other major offerings from companies including OpenAI and Anthropic.

hero.headline: SpaceX debuts at $150 a share in most anticipated IPO in years
hero.body:
SpaceX began trading on Friday at $150 per share, an 11 percent increase from its initial public offering price of $135. The debut marks the most anticipated stock market entry in recent history and caps years of growth for the aerospace company founded by Elon Musk.

The successful opening followed months of preparation documented in the company's S-1 registration filing. TechCrunch reported that the IPO process included examination of who stands to benefit from the public offering and analysis of pre-IPO deals that preceded the stock market debut.

The trading launch created immediate ripple effects across financial platforms. Robinhood reported record-breaking traffic as customers rushed to purchase shares, with some users experiencing intermittent disruptions that the platform said have since been resolved. The surge in trading activity demonstrated widespread public interest in accessing SpaceX stock.

The IPO also propelled Musk to a historic milestone. His stake in the newly public company pushed his total net worth above one trillion dollars, making him the first person to achieve trillionaire status. The valuation comes as Musk holds significant influence across multiple industries through his various business ventures.

SpaceX's market debut is part of a broader resurgence in technology company public offerings. The IPO market has returned with a different group of companies leading the charge, including artificial intelligence firms Anthropic and OpenAI, which are also preparing for public offerings in the same window. This wave of high-profile debuts represents a shift from the previous era dominated by established technology giants, testing investor appetite for a new generation of companies focused on space exploration and artificial intelligence.

cards.headline: Elon Musk becomes first trillionaire following SpaceX IPO
cards.teaser: The SpaceX founder's net worth surpassed one trillion dollars after the company's stock market debut.
cards.body:
SpaceX's initial public offering valued the company at $1.77 trillion after raising $75 billion through share sales. The offering boosted Musk's paper wealth past the $1 trillion mark, making him the world's first trillionaire. SpaceX was fast-tracked onto the Nasdaq index through recent rule changes by the exchange.

The IPO's strong performance is being supported by automatic buying pressure from tracker funds and index inclusion requirements. The offering marks a significant moment in the IPO market's resurgence, with space and artificial intelligence companies leading the charge ahead of traditional tech giants.

cards.headline: French AI startup Mistral seeks $3 billion at $23 billion valuation
cards.teaser: The funding round would nearly double the company's valuation from its previous financing.
cards.body:
Mistral is raising €3 billion at a €20 billion valuation, according to reports. This values the French AI startup at approximately $23.15 billion, nearly doubling its Series C funding round valuation of €11.7 billion.

The funding reflects strong investor appetite for AI companies as the sector experiences rapid growth and intensifying competition.

cards.headline: Google sues Chinese group over AI-powered text message scams
cards.teaser: The company alleges a cybercrime operation used artificial intelligence to send millions of fraudulent messages.
cards.body:
Google filed suit against Outsider Enterprise, a Chinese cybercrime group accused of using AI to conduct large-scale text message scams. The operation sent 2.5 million messages over two weeks, targeting hundreds of thousands of potential victims.

Google alleges the group used Gemini, its AI system, to automate the creation of fraudulent websites and messaging campaigns designed to steal money and personal information from recipients.

cards.headline: Protests halt $130 billion in data center construction this year
cards.teaser: Community opposition has blocked major infrastructure projects tied to AI expansion.
cards.body:
Data center projects worth $130 billion have been stopped by local protests in 2026. The opposition reflects growing resistance to large-scale infrastructure development linked to artificial intelligence computing needs.

Activists say the successful campaigns against data centers have given communities a sense of political power in shaping development decisions. The blocked projects represent a significant portion of planned AI infrastructure expansion as companies race to build computing capacity.

cards.headline: SpaceX, Anthropic, and OpenAI prepare simultaneous IPOs
cards.teaser: Three major technology companies are heading to public markets in the same period.
cards.body:
The IPO market is resurging with a new wave of companies leading the charge. Three major players—SpaceX, Anthropic, and OpenAI—are preparing public offerings in the same window, marking a shift away from the FAANG era.

Observers have coined the acronym MANGOS to describe this new generation of market leaders, which includes Meta, Anthropic, Nvidia, Google, OpenAI, and SpaceX. The simultaneous debuts of half these companies represent a significant test for investors evaluating valuations across artificial intelligence and aerospace sectors.

cards.headline: Robinhood experiences outages during SpaceX trading rush
cards.teaser: The platform saw record traffic as customers sought to purchase newly public shares.
cards.body:
Robinhood handled record-breaking traffic levels when SpaceX began trading publicly, marking the company's largest IPO to date. The surge reflected strong retail investor demand to buy shares in Elon Musk's aerospace company on its first day of public trading.

Some customers encountered intermittent disruptions while accessing the platform during the rush. Robinhood reported that the technical issues have since been resolved.

hero.headline: Kane Williamson retires from international cricket during England series
hero.body:
Kane Williamson has announced his retirement from international cricket effective immediately, bringing an end to a remarkable 16-year career that has spanned all formats of the game. The announcement came while New Zealand was actively competing in a Test series against England, meaning Williamson will not complete the current matches.

The 35-year-old finishes his international career as New Zealand's all-time leading run-scorer with 19,346 runs across 378 appearances, including 48 centuries. His Test record stands out as particularly impressive, with 110 matches played at an average of 54. Despite also finding success in limited-overs cricket, Test cricket remained his strongest format.

Williamson's final Test appearance came at Lord's, where he scored just 0 and 18 on a difficult batting surface. While the poor conditions contributed to his low scores, this match ultimately marked the end of his international involvement.

In a statement, Williamson explained his decision: "I've thought about it for a while, but over the last few days it's become clear now is the right time. I've always felt a strong drive and hunger for international cricket, and I take pride in knowing I've given it my all in every match I've played for New Zealand. Continuing with anything less wouldn't be right and I feel fortunate to step away on my own terms."

Williamson began his Test career in 2010 with a century on debut in Ahmedabad. He was later named one of cricket's most promising talents alongside Virat Kohli, Joe Root and Steve Smith. He topped the Test rankings for the first time in 2015 and was subsequently named a Wisden Cricketer of the Year.

His captaincy brought significant achievements, including leading New Zealand to victory in the inaugural World Test Championship final in 2021. He also guided his country to the T20 World Cup final in the same year, though they fell short against Australia. His leadership extended beyond international cricket, as he captained Sunrisers Hyderabad to the 2018 Indian Premier League final.

However, signs of his impending departure had emerged earlier. Williamson declined a New Zealand central contract in 2024, reducing his international commitments, and joined Lucknow Super Giants in the IPL in an advisory capacity.

New Zealand head coach Rob Walter praised Williamson's contributions: "His numbers and batting skills speak for themselves, but it's what he means to this Black Caps team, as well as world cricket - that will be his legacy. His impact on the culture and standards of this team will remain embedded in its DNA."

New Zealand will now face the remainder of the England series without one of their greatest players, heading to the Oval for the second Test already trailing 1-0.

cards.headline: Ghana midfielder Thomas Partey denied entry to Canada, misses World Cup opener
cards.teaser: Ghana will be without midfielder Thomas Partey for their opening World Cup match against Panama in Toronto.
cards.body:
Ghana midfielder Thomas Partey will miss his nation's opening World Cup match after being denied entry to Canada. The former Arsenal player was unable to travel to Toronto for Ghana's group stage fixture against Panama.

Partey's absence is a significant blow to Ghana's midfield as they begin their World Cup campaign. The denial of entry removes one of the team's key players from the opening match.

cards.headline: Judge allows UFC event at White House to proceed
cards.teaser: A federal judge rejected a legal challenge seeking to cancel a UFC event scheduled at the White House this weekend.
cards.body:
A federal judge has refused to block a UFC event scheduled for this weekend at the White House. US District Judge Amit Mehta ruled against Virginia residents who challenged the Trump administration's authority to host the mixed martial arts competition on the South Lawn.

The event is set to take place Sunday and will celebrate both the nation's 250th anniversary and President Trump's 80th birthday. An elaborate arena has already been constructed on the White House grounds for the fight.

cards.headline: Manchester United secures new $550 million funding deal with higher interest rates
cards.teaser: Manchester United agreed to new financing that will increase the cost of servicing the club's debt.
cards.body:
Manchester United has agreed a new $550 million funding deal that will increase the club's debt servicing costs. The interest rate on the financing has risen from 3.79% to 5.36%, meaning the club will pay significantly more each year to service its debt obligations.

The higher borrowing costs reflect the current interest rate environment as Manchester United refinances its existing debt through this new arrangement.

cards.headline: Scotland's Scott McTominay available for World Cup opener after illness
cards.teaser: The midfielder returned to training after missing the previous session due to an upset stomach.
cards.body:
Scotland midfielder Scott McTominay returned to training on the eve of the World Cup opener against Haiti, after missing the previous day's session with an upset stomach.

McTominay confirmed he is ready to play in Scotland's first match of the tournament, providing a welcome boost to the squad ahead of their clash with Haiti.

cards.headline: Emma Raducanu and Katie Boulter advance to Queen's quarter-finals
cards.teaser: Both British players recorded wins to reach the quarter-finals at the Queen's Club tournament.
cards.body:
Emma Raducanu and Katie Boulter have both advanced to the quarter-finals at Queen's Club Championship. Raducanu secured her spot with a dominant straight-set victory over Romania's Sorana Cirstea.

Both British players will face a demanding schedule, as they are required to play their quarter-final matches on the same day they won their previous rounds.

cards.headline: Lando Norris edges George Russell in Barcelona practice
cards.teaser: McLaren's Norris topped the timing sheets in Friday practice ahead of Russell's Mercedes.
cards.body:
Lando Norris finished ahead of George Russell during Friday practice at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix. The McLaren driver topped the day's running ahead of the Mercedes competitor.

Norris expressed optimism about McLaren's prospects at the circuit, hoping the team will demonstrate stronger performance in Barcelona as the season progresses.

hero.headline: British Artist David Hockney Dies at 88
hero.body:
David Hockney, the legendary British painter whose vibrant works helped define contemporary art across seven decades, has died at 88. He passed away peacefully at home on June 11, 2026, just one month before his 89th birthday.

Hockney rose to prominence during the 1960s as a pop artist and became internationally recognized for his swimming pool paintings that captured the essence of Los Angeles life. Works such as "A Bigger Splash" and "Portrait of an Artist (Pool With Two Figures)" depicted scenes of desire and loss beneath California's bright skies. The latter painting became one of the most expensive works by a living artist when it sold at auction in 2018.

Born in Bradford, West Yorkshire, in 1937, Hockney came from what he described as a "radical working-class family." He studied at Bradford College and London's Royal College of Art, where he developed a reputation as a talented but rebellious artist. He famously submitted a work called "Life Drawing for a Diploma" instead of painting a required female model, depicting a male figure from an American physique magazine instead. The college bent its rules to award him his diploma.

Throughout his career, Hockney refused to accept artistic boundaries. His 1961 painting "We Two Boys Together Clinging," named after a Walt Whitman poem, depicted gay relationships with unprecedented honesty at a time when homosexuality remained illegal in Britain. Later works continued exploring themes of queer life with openness and wit.

Beyond swimming pools, Hockney's work encompassed perspective-shifting photo-collage portraits, abstract landscape paintings, and experiments with emerging digital technologies including iPad and 3D art creation. He remained constantly inventive, producing new work throughout his eighth decade.

King Charles paid tribute to Hockney as "a giant of the world of art and painting, a Yorkshireman through and through." The king noted Hockney's "irrepressible charm, talent and constant innovation," recalling how the artist wore his signature yellow Crocs to a Palace occasion.

Tracey Emin described Hockney as "a great artist and a wonderful man, who with the power of art changed the perception of Britishness." Prime Minister Keir Starmer said his "vivid, instantly recognisable work influenced generations of artists."

The Tate Britain director Alex Farquharson called Hockney "an endlessly inventive artist" who "taught us about the joy of looking, seeing things the rest of us failed to notice." The Tate plans to stage a major exhibition of his work next year, along with a multimedia installation at Tate Modern.

Hockney is survived by his long-time partner Jean-Pierre Gonçalves de Lima, his brothers Philip and John, and numerous relatives. His publicist said his enduring legacy reflects "his underlying enthusiasm for life" and his signature phrase: "Love Life."

cards.headline: Elon Musk Becomes First Trillionaire After SpaceX IPO
cards.teaser: The SpaceX CEO is now worth more than three times the world's second-richest person following his rocket company's public offering.
cards.body:
Elon Musk's net worth surpassed $1 trillion following SpaceX's initial public offering on the stock market. The rocket company's IPO was valued at $1.77 trillion and raised $75 billion through share offerings, marking one of the largest public offerings in recent years.

The Nasdaq fast-tracked SpaceX's inclusion on the index, generating significant buying pressure from tracker funds and other institutional investors that are required to purchase shares in newly listed companies. Musk's wealth now exceeds that of the world's second-richest person by a substantial margin.

cards.headline: Court Orders Justin Baldoni to Pay Blake Lively's Legal Fees
cards.teaser: A court has ruled that actor Justin Baldoni must cover Blake Lively's legal expenses in their ongoing case.
cards.body:
A court has ruled that Justin Baldoni must cover Blake Lively's legal fees in their ongoing dispute. The order requires Baldoni to pay for the costs associated with Lively's legal representation throughout the case.

This judicial decision marks a notable turn in the legal proceedings between the two actors.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Releases Third Studio Album with Target Exclusives
cards.teaser: The singer's new album "You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love" is now available with special-edition vinyl versions at Target.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo's third studio album, "You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love," is now available worldwide. The release has generated significant attention, with listeners and media outlets closely examining the album's lyrics for personal details about the singer's life.

Target is offering exclusive vinyl variants of the album as part of a partnership with Rodrigo, making the retail chain a key outlet for fans seeking special editions.

cards.headline: Michael Jackson Abuse Case Gets 2028 Trial Date
cards.teaser: Wade Robson and James Safechuck will have their case against the late pop star heard in 2028.
cards.body:
A new trial date has been set for 2028 in the case involving Wade Robson and James Safechuck against Michael Jackson's estate. The two men claim the late pop star sexually abused them when they were minors.

The case has been ongoing for years, with previous court proceedings and appeals. The 2028 date represents the next scheduled hearing for the allegations against Jackson, who died in 2009.

cards.headline: Jimmi Simpson Joins Elisabeth Moss in Hulu's 'Conviction'
cards.teaser: The actor will star in the upcoming drama series based on Jack Jordan's novel.
cards.body:
Jimmi Simpson has been cast in the Hulu drama series "Conviction," joining previously announced lead Elisabeth Moss. Simpson will appear alongside Sebastian De Souza and Adam Godley in the production.

The show is based on Jack Jordan's novel of the same name. Hulu greenlit the series in February, and production is moving forward with the expanded cast.

cards.headline: Tom Cruise Attends 'Disclosure Day' Screening with Spielberg Co-Stars
cards.teaser: The actor reunited with Colin Farrell and Dakota Fanning for a screening of Steven Spielberg's new alien thriller.
cards.body:
Tom Cruise reunited with Steven Spielberg collaborators Colin Farrell and Dakota Fanning at a screening of the director's new alien thriller "Disclosure Day." Cruise previously starred alongside Farrell in "Minority Report" and worked with Fanning on "War of the Worlds," both Spielberg-directed films.

The screening brought together actors from across Spielberg's filmography to celebrate the release of his latest project.

hero.headline: Pakistan announces US and Iran reach agreement to end conflict
hero.body:
Pakistan's prime minister declared on Friday that the United States and Iran have reached an agreement on a peace framework to end their conflict, which has lasted more than 100 days. Pakistan has been leading mediation efforts between the two countries to halt hostilities in the Middle East and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

The announcement came after President Donald Trump stated that the two nations were on the verge of signing a peace agreement and cancelled planned missile strikes on Iran. However, Iranian officials quickly challenged Trump's characterization of the deal's status, creating conflicting narratives about whether a final agreement had actually been reached.

Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said that "exchanges of messages are continuing, but no final agreement has been reached yet." The semi-official Tasnim news agency reported that Trump's announcement was "in line with his usual pattern of making unilateral and egotistical statements."

Trump outlined his conditions for the deal on his Truth Social platform, stating that Iran "must agree that they will never have a Nuclear Weapon or Bomb." He also listed opening the Strait of Hormuz for all traffic without tolls, eliminating mines in the waterway, and allowing the United States to remove and destroy highly enriched uranium from a secure nuclear site in Iran. The deal would also block the transfer of frozen assets to Iran, according to Trump.

Vice President JD Vance pushed back against details that Iranian officials had leaked about the proposed agreement, insisting that Iran would not receive any cash under its terms. The Trump administration dismissed information that Tehran had released about the possible memorandum of understanding.

Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi struck a more optimistic tone, stating that an agreement to extend the ceasefire, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and launch negotiations on Iran's nuclear program has "never been closer to completion." His remarks represented the most hopeful assessment yet from Tehran about finalizing a deal in the coming days.

Iran's top negotiator Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf sent a defiant message, stating that "we seize concessions not through dialogue, but with missiles." He also warned that Iran was ready for another round of fighting if talks to extend the ceasefire failed.

The proposed framework addresses multiple aspects of the conflict between the two nations. Beyond ending immediate hostilities, the agreement would tackle access through the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for global oil shipments. Discussions on Iran's nuclear program indicate the diplomatic effort extends beyond the military confrontation to address longer-term security concerns that have defined US-Iran relations for decades.

A meeting in Washington between US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar ended without public comment on the negotiations.

cards.headline: Federal judge denies request to pause Trump name removal from Kennedy Center
cards.teaser: A judge rejected President Trump's request to delay a ruling requiring his name to be removed from the Kennedy Center.
cards.body:
A federal judge rejected President Trump's last-minute request to pause an order requiring his name be removed from the Kennedy Center. The ruling allows the facility to proceed with the removal as originally ordered, with compliance required on the same day the motion was denied.

The decision means the Kennedy Center must move forward with taking down Trump's name from the building and its signage.

cards.headline: Judge rules Virginia residents lack standing to challenge White House UFC event
cards.teaser: A federal judge dismissed a lawsuit seeking to block this weekend's UFC fight on the White House South Lawn.
cards.body:
U.S. District Judge Amit Mehta ruled Friday that Virginia residents lack legal standing to challenge the UFC event scheduled for the White House South Lawn this weekend. The judge denied their request to block the mixed martial arts show, allowing organizers to proceed with the event.

The UFC event, branded "UFC Freedom 250," coincides with the nation's 250th anniversary celebration and President Trump's 80th birthday. An elaborate arena has already been constructed on the South Lawn for the Sunday fight. Motocross athlete Travis Pastrana is scheduled to perform a stunt on the lawn the day before the UFC event.

cards.headline: House Oversight requests Alan Dershowitz testify in Epstein investigation
cards.teaser: The House committee asked the criminal defense lawyer to answer questions about his representation of Jeffrey Epstein.
cards.body:
The House Oversight Committee requested that Alan Dershowitz testify in its investigation related to Jeffrey Epstein. Dershowitz, a criminal defense lawyer, previously represented Epstein in legal matters.

Dershowitz said he would be open to answering the committee's questions. The request is part of the committee's ongoing probe into matters connected to Epstein.

cards.headline: Pentagon releases UFO files including witness video recreations
cards.teaser: The latest batch of UFO files from the Defense Department includes artistic renderings created by witnesses.
cards.body:
The Pentagon released its latest collection of UFO files, which includes video recreations of sightings. The files contain artistic renderings produced by individuals the Pentagon deemed credible witnesses.

The release represents the most recent disclosure of government records related to unidentified flying objects. The inclusion of witness-created recreations marks a different approach from previous file releases that focused primarily on official government documentation and sensor data.

cards.headline: Lawsuit challenges city ordinance requiring permit for home prayer
cards.teaser: An Orthodox Jewish man filed suit after being denied the right to pray in his home without a special permit.
cards.body:
Daniel Grand, an Orthodox Jew, filed a lawsuit alleging a First Amendment violation after a city ordinance denied him the right to pray in his home without obtaining a special-use permit. The case has drawn attention to government restrictions on religious practice in private residences.

The lawsuit highlights a division among federal appeals courts regarding when citizens can access federal courts to challenge such restrictions. The case raises questions about the extent to which local governments can regulate religious activities conducted in private homes.

cards.headline: Shooter and one victim killed in Texas incident
cards.teaser: Police said the active shooter situation ended hours after gunfire erupted in Midland.
cards.body:
A shooting in Midland, Texas on Friday resulted in one death and nine others hospitalized with injuries. The suspected shooter engaged in a two-hour standoff with police before being found dead later that afternoon, according to city authorities and the police department.

The incident unfolded across multiple locations in Midland, beginning in one area before moving near a veterinary hospital. Law enforcement responded to the active shooter situation, which concluded on Friday afternoon.
